bq1.matching_rule: Scan every string leaf returned by yaml.safe_load over the six held files. An occurrence is recorded when a regex match captures (a) a deictic/definite description whose head noun is a document-ish word (file, layer, contract, specification, amendment, protocol, text, experiment, record, table, convention, document, report, decision, hypothesis, yaml, stack, receipt, manifest, artifact, design, transcript, source) optionally qualified by held/combined/governing, or the bare deictics above/below/following/the following; (b) a repository-relative path or AMD-*/specification.yaml/EXP-AUXIN-7e2e3d token; or (c) an amendment.<path> or experiment.<path> form. Matching is case-insensitive for (a). Overlapping matches: prefer the longest match at each start offset; do not double-count nested captures of the same span. Character offset is 0-based within the leaf string as the YAML safe loader returned it.

rows.effective_text: "prime" means prime in the mathematical sense. A search accepts a candidate only if every integer its acceptance rule names is prime. OPERATIONAL SCREEN: the Baillie-PSW test, defined as a strong probable-prime test to base 2 followed by a strong Lucas probable-prime test with Selfridge method A parameters (D is the first of 5, -7, 9, -11, 13, ... with Jacobi symbol (D/n) = -1; P = 1; Q = (1 - D)/4). Trial division by small primes may precede it; that cannot change which candidate is first accepted (conventions.Q0-5). PROOF: every accepted integer is then proved prime by a certificate under change.D7_certificates. If a candidate passes the screen but its certificate run proves it composite, it is NOT accepted, the search continues from the next candidate, and the event is recorded. If the certificate run fails without proving compositeness, that is an infrastructure stop, never a skip.

rows.effective_text: For a prime r and a branch b in {minus, plus}, let m_minus = r - 1 and m_plus = r + 1. For a positive divisor d of m_b: T_minus(d) = sqrt(m_minus / d) + sqrt(d)   (Cheon 2006 Theorem 1 leading expression); T_plus(d)  = sqrt(m_plus / d) + d          (Cheon 2006 Theorem 2 leading expression; Theorem 2, not the 2006 abstract). e_b(d) = log2(T_b(d)) / log2(r). Admissible d is every positive divisor of m_b, including 1 and m_b. The two branches are never combined: no quantity in this amendment is a minimum over both branches.
clauses: via=incorporates.sha256 of AMD-20260927-narrow.yaml, through incorporates_by_hash of this file

rows.via: incorporates.sha256 of AMD-20260927-narrow.yaml, through incorporates_by_hash of this file
rows.effective_text: F_minus(r) = (1 + log2(r - 1)/4) / log2(r), the exact minimum over real x > 0 of log2(sqrt(m_minus/x) + sqrt(x)) / log2(r). F_plus(r) = (log2(3) - 2/3 + log2(r + 1)/3) / log2(r), the exact minimum over real x > 0 of log2(sqrt(m_plus/x) + x) / log2(r), attained at x = (m_plus/4)^(1/3), called the T_plus optimum. C_b(r) = log2(sqrt(m_b) + 1) / log2(r), the value at d = 1 on either branch.
clauses: via=incorporates.sha256 of AMD-20260927-narrow.yaml, through incorporates_by_hash of this file

rows.effective_text: For a REPORTED BRANCH VALUE e on branch b (an EXACT branch minimum or a BOUND witnessed upper bound), depth s = (C_b(r) - e) / (C_b(r) - F_b(r)). Because d = 1 is a candidate in every divisor set and every witness set, and F_b is the real minimum, every reported branch value satisfies F_b(r) <= e <= C_b(r) mathematically, so s lies in [0, 1]. A single e_b(d) at an arbitrary d need not lie in that range and is never binned. s near 1 means a divisor near the branch's analytic optimum; s near 0 means none.

rows.effective_text: For an EXACT value the rules are applied IN THIS ORDER and the first that applies gives the bin: (i) if boundary_flag is true, the value takes the bin on its lower-depth side, so s within tau of 3/4 gives INTERMEDIATE and s within tau of 1/4 gives NEAR_CEILING; (ii) NEAR_FLOOR if s >= 3/4 + tau; (iii) NEAR_CEILING if s <= 1/4 - tau; (iv) INTERMEDIATE otherwise. PRECEDENCE: the flag rule (i) precedes the cut-off rules (ii) and (iii). So s = 3/4 + tau exactly is flagged and gives INTERMEDIATE, s = 1/4 - tau exactly is flagged and gives NEAR_CEILING, and no s receives two bins.

Let tau = 10^-45, an ABSOLUTE tolerance on s (conventions.Q0-8). boundary_flag is true if |s - 1/4| <= tau or |s - 3/4| <= tau, else false.  For a BOUND value see change.D3_descriptive_bins.bin_by_status. Bins carry no stop, escalate, naming or decision semantics (change.D4_calibration).

TIE RULE, relative in the exponent e (conventions.Q0-7): a divisor d is tied if e_b(d) - e* <= 10^-100 * e*. The reported minimiser is the SMALLEST tied divisor. On the minus branch d and m_minus/d always tie exactly, so the smaller member of that pair is reported.

rows.effective_text: (conventions.Q0-9.) Every gate inequality is evaluated numerically at the precision floor above, on path A and on path B separately. A lower gate of the form "0 <= e - F" is evaluated as e - F >= -10^-45, the same slack as change.D2_typed_costs.floor_invariant. An upper gate of the form "e - F <= c" is evaluated as e - F <= c with no slack. A gate holds only if it holds on both paths; if the two paths return different verdicts on any gate, the run stops with outcome N1 for a construction control, N2 for a C-FIELD gate, or N4 for a C-BOUND gate, because the instrument is then not determinate at its own precision.

rows.effective_text: (NIST SP 800-186, derived text inputs/SAFECURVES-20260825/specs/sp800-186.txt.) BLOCK: from the first line whose stripped content equals the section number given for the row (for example "3.2.1.3.") to, exclusive, the next line whose stripped content matches the regular expression ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)*\.$ . LABEL LINE for label L (L is p, h or n): the first line in the block whose content, after removing leading whitespace-set characters, begins with the two characters "L:". SPAN: from the character after "L:" to, exclusive, the earlier of (a) the first "(" character after "L:" and (b) the start of the next line in the block whose stripped content matches ^[A-Za-z]{1,4}: . DECIMAL FORM: the span with the whitespace set and backslashes removed; it is CLEAN if it is non-empty and consists of decimal digits only, otherwise CONTAMINATED (for example a printed expression whose superscripts or minus signs were lost, or interleaved page text) and it is then ignored and recorded as contaminated. HEX FORM: exists only if case (a) ended the span and, after that "(" and with the whitespace set removed, the next three characters are "=0x"; it runs from after "=0x" to, exclusive, the first ")" after it; with the whitespace set removed it is CLEAN if non-empty and hex digits only, otherwise CONTAMINATED and ignored. VALUE: if the hex form is clean, the value is its base-16 integer V. The decimal form is then compared only if it is clean AND has exactly as many digits as the decimal expansion of V: in that case it must equal V, else locator_failure. A clean decimal form with a different digit count is a printed expression whose operators were lost in the derived text (for example an exponent expression printed without its superscript and minus sign); it is recorded as decimal_span_not_a_literal and ignored. If the hex form is absent or contaminated and the decimal form is clean, the value is the decimal integer. If neither is clean, locator_failure. Which representation was used, and every ignored span with its reason, is recorded.

Every row, cross-source or C-FIELD comparison that reads a derived .txt file (sp800-186.txt or sec2-v2.txt) is digit-checked against the authoritative PDF named in inputs/SAFECURVES-20260825/source_record.yaml (sp800-186.pdf, sec2-v2.pdf), whose sha256 is bound above. A FAIL makes the row UNPINNED with reason pdf_digit_mismatch (or, for a cross-source, a cross-source failure). The extracted normalized text is archived as sources/<pdf-name>.normalized.txt with its sha256, and every verdict is written to pdf_check.json.

rows.effective_text: J. H. Cheon, Security Analysis of the Strong Diffie-Hellman Problem, EUROCRYPT 2006, LNCS 4004. Theorem 1: for d | p - 1, given g, g^alpha and g^(alpha^d), alpha is computed in O(log p * (sqrt((p-1)/d) + sqrt(d))) group operations. Theorem 2 (the theorem statement, not the 2006 abstract, whose "i = 0, 1, ..., d" is not followed): for d | p + 1, given the 2d consecutive powers g^(alpha^i), i = 1..2d, alpha is computed in O(log p * (sqrt((p+1)/d) + d)) group operations. Here p is the prime group order, called r in this experiment. The J. Cryptology 2010 version (Discrete Logarithm Problems with Auxiliary Inputs) states the same leading expressions with an Exp_G(p) factor, the linear d term on p + 1, and i = 1..2d.

rows.via: AMD-20260927-narrow.yaml span_rules[F2-RECOG].replacement
rows.effective_text: The call is evaluated by the cypari2 Pari instance of corrective.tools.certificate_and_factoring_library.stack_allocation, as p("alarm(A, factor(n))") with A and n written in decimal. RECOGNITION, in this order: (i) if the call raises cysignals.signals.AlarmInterrupt, caught by naming that class, the call timed out (that class derives from KeyboardInterrupt, not from Exception, so a handler for Exception does not catch it); (ii) if the call returns a PARI object of type t_ERROR whose errname is e_ALARM (the gp-interface form of the same event), the call timed out; in case (i) or (ii) the part stays unfactored and the timeout is recorded together with which form was observed; (iii) if the call returns an object of type t_MAT, the call completed and that matrix is its factorization; (iv) any other exception, any other return type, or termination of the process by a signal is a crash under stopping_rules (memory protection or crash), never a timeout. After (i) or (ii) the same Pari instance serves later calls; admission item (3) checks that it remains usable.

rows.effective_text: F2 (in-process PARI): each call is issued as the GP expression alarm(A, factor(n)) with A = floor(R) seconds; if floor(R) < 1 the call is not made and the part stays unfactored.  F3 (GMP-ECM subprocess): each subprocess is started with a hard timeout of R seconds (killed on expiry, which is recorded). Any overrun of an alarm or kill beyond R is charged to the integer, is recorded, and is never refunded. No other timeout mechanism is used.

rows.effective_text: F0 trial division of m_b by every prime below 2^24. F1 every remaining part is tested for being a perfect power (and split if so) and screened for primality; prime parts go to certification and leave the pipeline. F2 every composite part of at most 272 bits goes to PARI factor() under the F2 timeout above; parts are processed in ascending size. F3 every composite part of more than 272 bits goes to GMP-ECM, run over the B1 ladder in ascending order with the fixed number of curves per level below, invoked as "ecm -one -c <curves> <B1>" with the part on standard input, repeating the last level if the ladder completes. After each ECM subprocess returns, every factor it reports that divides the part is split off; every resulting piece re-enters F1, and any composite piece of at most 272 bits goes to F2. For a piece that remains above 272 bits the ladder resumes at the level where it stopped, counting the curves already run at that level. The 272-bit value routes a part between two methods; it never ends the budget.
clauses: via=incorporates.sha256 of AMD-20260927-narrow.yaml, through incorporates_by_hash of this file

For each prime p < 2^64, and for the terminal prime of every ECPP chain: a Pratt certificate, built by path A from the complete factorization of p - 1 (recursively, to the leaf 2) with a witness a. PARI's primecert returns a bare integer, not a certificate, for p < 2^64; that return is never treated as a certificate.

rows.effective_text: A NEW library-free module, experiments/EXP-AUXIN-7e2e3d/implementation/typed/cert_verify.py, importing only the Python standard library (checked by the AST import audit at admission). It shares no code with PARI, GMP-ECM, FLINT, pypdf or sympy. Its version is the sha256 of its bytes at the launch commit. It checks. (i) Pratt: the listed prime powers multiply to p - 1; a^(p-1) = 1 mod p; a^((p-1)/f) != 1 mod p for each listed prime f; each f carries its own valid certificate. (ii) ECPP step with (N, t, s, a4, P = (x, y)): gcd(N, 6) = 1; m = N + 1 - t; s divides m and q = m/s; b = y^2 - x^3 - a4*x mod N; gcd(4*a4^3 + 27*b^2, N) = 1; [m]P is the point at infinity and [s]P is an affine point whose denominators are invertible mod N, both by exact arithmetic mod N; q > (c + 1)^2 where c is the least integer with c^4 >= N; the next step's N equals q; the chain's terminal q carries a valid Pratt certificate. (iii) Compositeness witnesses: the recorded base a is the smallest integer a >= 2 for which C fails the strong probable-prime test to base a (such a base exists for every odd composite C, including Carmichael numbers); the verifier re-runs that strong test. An even composite part has witness 2 recorded as "even". This arithmetic runs on auxiliary curves over Z/NZ for primality proofs only; it involves no curve of the frozen list and no auxiliary-input power.

rows.effective_text: Stated in advance, each by an argument from the recipe alone. (a) ROUTING. f1, f2, f3, f4 and w all exceed 2^24, so F0 removes only 2^2 * 3 from r + 1, and the remaining part f1*f2*f3*f4*w has more than 272 bits (its log2 is about B_L - log2(12), far above 272), so the pipeline must send it to F3. (b) MINIMISER. D_L lies in [x_L, x_L * (1 + 2^-19)), because D_L = G * f4 >= G * y >= x_L and D_L < G * (y + 2^24) <= x_L + G * (1 + 2^24), where G is about 2^129 and x_L is about 2^172. And (r + 1)/4 differs from M_L/4 by a relative amount below 2^-290 (w < w0 + 2^48). So D_L is within a relative 2^-18 of the T_plus optimum x = ((r + 1)/4)^(1/3). Write T_plus(t*x) = x * (2/sqrt(t) + t), minimised only at t = 1 with value 3x. Every divisor of r + 1 is s * (product of a subset of {f1, f2, f3, f4}) * w^c with s | 12 and c in {0, 1}. With c = 1 the divisor exceeds w, which is above 2^300, so T_plus > 2^300. With c = 0 and at most three of the f_i, the divisor is below 12 * 2^133, so t < 2^-35 and T_plus > 2^17 * x. With all four f_i the divisor is s * D_L, with t within 2^-18 of s, and 2/sqrt(t) + t is least at s = 1 (value 3 + O(2^-36)), against at least 2/sqrt(2) + 2 > 3.41 for s >= 2. Hence the plus minimiser is D_L, uniquely, and e_plus - F_plus is below 10^-6 by a wide margin. (c) MINUS BRANCH. r - 1 = 2q with q prime, so the minimiser is the smaller member of the tied pair {2, q}, and its depth is below 1/4 by the same inequality as C-BOUND BND-2 (argument there).

rows.effective_text: {"change.D6_factoring":{"budget":"Each integer m_b (every branch of every construction control, null-arm and deployed row) receives the full factoring_seconds_per_integer = 3600 seconds. Factoring stops only when m_b is completely factored or that budget is spent. THERE IS NO BIT CAP: no integer and no part is excluded from any stage by its size.","budget_semantics":"A BOUND row means the full budget was spent without completing the factorization. It is not a statement that the integer resists factoring, and it is never negative evidence (core rule 5).","clock":"(F-J1-5, entry 9.) The budget clock is the executor process's monotonic wall clock (Python time.monotonic()), read immediately before and after every factoring call on a part, whether the call runs in-process (PARI through cypari2) or in a subprocess (GMP-ECM). The seconds charged to an integer are the sum of those intervals over all its parts and stages. The remaining budget R is 3600 minus the seconds charged so far.","ecm_curves_per_level":"(F-J1-3, entry 8.) DECLARED CONSTANTS of this protocol, not read from the installed tool: B1 = 2e3: 25 curves; 11e3: 90; 5e4: 300; 25e4: 700; 1e6: 1800; 3e6: 5100; 11e6: 10600; 43e6: 19300; 11e7: 49000; 26e7: 124000; 85e7: 210000; after the last level, 85e7 is repeated with 210000 curves per repetition until the budget is spent. Provenance: the values follow the GMP-ECM README's expected-curves table as recalled by this design session (provenance recalled, a pointer only). The protocol does not depend on that recollection being exact, because the column is a declared constant, not a claim about the tool.","ecm_nondeterminism_disclosure":"GMP-ECM draws its own curve parameters (sigma), which are recorded per curve. Which composite parts a re-run splits within the budget may therefore differ, which can change EXACT versus BOUND on a deployed or null-arm branch. A certified factorization and every value derived from it never change.","pipeline":"F0 trial division of m_b by every prime below 2^24. F1 every remaining part is tested for being a perfect power (and split if so) and screened for primality; prime parts go to certification and leave the pipeline. F2 every composite part of at most 272 bits goes to PARI factor() under the F2 timeout above; parts are processed in ascending size. F3 every composite part of more than 272 bits goes to GMP-ECM, run over the B1 ladder in ascending order with the fixed number of curves per level below, invoked as \"ecm -one -c <curves> <B1>\" with the part on standard input, repeating the last level if the ladder completes. After each ECM subprocess returns, every factor it reports that divides the part is split off; every resulting piece re-enters F1, and any composite piece of at most 272 bits goes to F2. For a piece that remains above 272 bits the ladder resumes at the level where it stopped, counting the curves already run at that level. The 272-bit value routes a part between two methods; it never ends the budget.","reporting":"(F-J1-4, entry 9.) Per integer: the list of parts it passed through, each identified by its decimal value, bit length and the stage that produced it; for EACH part, seconds charged in each of F0 to F3; the ECM curves run at each B1 level with their sigma values and seconds; every F2 alarm and F3 kill; the final list of certified prime powers; and the recorded composite parts with bit lengths, compositeness witnesses and perfect-power checks. Certificate generation is timed separately and is not charged to the factoring budget.","timeouts":"F2 (in-process PARI): each call is issued as the GP expression alarm(A, factor(n)) with A = floor(R) seconds; if floor(R) < 1 the call is not made and the part stays unfactored. An alarm return (PARI error e_ALARM) means the call timed out; the part stays unfactored and the timeout is recorded. F3 (GMP-ECM subprocess): each subprocess is started with a hard timeout of R seconds (killed on expiry, which is recorded). Any overrun of an alarm or kill beyond R is charged to the integer, is recorded, and is never refunded. No other timeout mechanism is used."},"change.D7_certificates":{"changes_from_d1d10_with_reason":"The module path moves from implementation/d1d10/ to implementation/typed/ (change.D10_additivity). The check gcd(N, 6) = 1 is added and the compositeness witness becomes a strong-test witness; both close gaps VAL-20260923-c3c90c attack_iii recorded (the omitted gcd check and the Carmichael case). Nothing else changes.","criterion_provenance":"The Goldwasser-Kilian and Atkin-Morain step criterion, Pratt's criterion and the existence of a strong-test witness for every odd composite are recalled by this design session (provenance recalled, pointer, not support). VAL-20260923-c3c90c attack_iii records a worked soundness check of the step criterion (internal). The admission self-tests are what the run relies on.","independent_verifier":"A NEW library-free module, experiments/EXP-AUXIN-7e2e3d/implementation/typed/cert_verify.py, importing only the Python standard library (checked by the AST import audit at admission). (i) Pratt: the listed prime powers multiply to p - 1; a^(p-1) = 1 mod p; a^((p-1)/f) != 1 mod p for each listed prime f; each f carries its own valid certificate. (ii) ECPP step with (N, t, s, a4, P = (x, y)): gcd(N, 6) = 1; m = N + 1 - t; s divides m and q = m/s; b = y^2 - x^3 - a4*x mod N; gcd(4*a4^3 + 27*b^2, N) = 1; [m]P is the point at infinity and [s]P is an affine point whose denominators are invertible mod N, both by exact arithmetic mod N; q > (c + 1)^2 where c is the least integer with c^4 >= N; the next step's N equals q; the chain's terminal q carries a valid Pratt certificate. (iii) Compositeness witnesses: the recorded base a is the smallest integer a >= 2 for which C fails the strong probable-prime test to base a (such a base exists for every odd composite C, including Carmichael numbers); the verifier re-runs that strong test. An even composite part has witness 2 recorded as \"even\". This arithmetic runs on auxiliary curves over Z/NZ for primality proofs only; it involves no curve of the frozen list and no auxiliary-input power.","producing_library":"PARI/GP through cypari2. rows.effective_text: {"applies_to":"EVERY deployed row, before any factoring; every C-FIELD case; every construction-control integer; every null-arm integer.","clauses_in_order":"(1) field_prime: REJECT if the candidate equals ANY member of the field-prime set FP, defined as every field prime extracted in Stage P for any row (whether or not that row pinned) together with the two C-FIELD expression values. For a deployed row this includes its own extracted field prime. (2) not_prime: REJECT unless the candidate is proved prime under change.D7_certificates. (3) hasse: applies only to a deployed row or C-FIELD case whose source prints a cofactor h; REJECT unless |p + 1 - h*r| <= 2*isqrt(p) + 2, where p and h are that row's extracted field prime and cofactor and r is the candidate.","evaluation_and_recording":"(entry 4.) All applicable clauses are evaluated, in the order above, on every candidate; evaluation never stops at the first reason. The result is the ordered list of reasons that fired, written to confounder_receipt.json per candidate, together with the verdict of each clause. The candidate is REJECTED if and only if the list is non-empty. A rejected deployed row is invalid_measurement for that row and is never factored.","scope_on_controls_and_null_arm":"(conventions.Q0-3.) For construction controls and null-arm integers there is no \"same curve\": clause (1) compares against the whole set FP, clause (2) applies, and clause (3) does not apply because no source prints a cofactor for them. The expected outcome for every construction control is NOT REJECTED (no reason). If a construction control is rejected, the run stops with outcome I_CONTROL_COLLISION (never N1, never a result), because a constructed control that equals an extracted field prime is a defect of this text's recipes. A rejected null-arm sample is kept, flagged and not factored.","tested_by":"controls C-FIELD and C-FIELD-MUTATION, in Stage P, before any row is pinned."}

rows.effective_text: For a prime r and a branch b in {minus, plus}, let m_minus = r - 1 and m_plus = r + 1. For a positive divisor d of m_b: T_minus(d) = sqrt(m_minus / d) + sqrt(d)   (Cheon 2006 Theorem 1 leading expression); T_plus(d)  = sqrt(m_plus / d) + d          (Cheon 2006 Theorem 2 leading expression; Theorem 2, not the 2006 abstract). e_b(d) = log2(T_b(d)) / log2(r). Admissible d is every positive divisor of m_b, including 1 and m_b. The two branches are never combined: no quantity in this amendment is a minimum over both branches.

rows.effective_text: {"change.D9_labelling":{"applies_to":"every artifact of the run, the execution report and any record that cites the run.","rule":"Per CORR-20260923-187ea3 labelling_rule_for_any_citing_record, with the unit statement of CORR-20260923-f5f060. The rho column is named rho_ordinary_input, value 0.5 (the frozen rho_baseline), and is annotated as the ordinary-input cost exponent of a different problem. Every typed exponent column name ends in E_ASSUMES_AUXILIARY_INPUT and names its branch. Every row states per branch the input model, the condition label and the bits of d (change.D2_typed_costs). The table header cites DEC-20260802-204 B032-C7 and B032-C8. The phrase \"identical accounting\" does not appear in any artifact. The supply condition is stated in the header: every typed exponent is conditional on the named auxiliary input being supplied, which this experiment does not examine (IDEA-20260831-ccb587 unopened).","secondary_metric_scope":"(entry 12, O3/S3.) The quantity \"bits of the largest divisor of m_b not exceeding isqrt(r)\" is reported on the MINUS branch only, labelled \"arithmetic; on the minus branch it locates the divisor nearest the T_minus optimum\". It is not computed or reported on the plus branch, where a divisor near sqrt(r) prices at T_plus >= d and is not a Theorem-2 quantity.","unit_statement_beside_rho":"(entry 11.) Printed verbatim in the typed_table header immediately beside rho_ordinary_input, and in the execution report: \"The typed exponents are exponents of the leading step-count expressions of Cheon's Theorems 1 and 2. Each step is an exponentiation: the theorems carry an O(log p) group-operation factor (EUROCRYPT 2006) or an Exp_G(p) factor (J. Cryptology 2010). The typed exponents omit that factor and the O() constants, so they understate group-operation counts. The rho exponent counts group operations. The two units differ by a factor Theta(log r).\" No artifact, report or citing record states that the typed exponents and the rho exponent are in the same unit."},"definitions.typed_costs":"For a prime r and a branch b in {minus, plus}, let m_minus = r - 1 and m_plus = r + 1. For a positive divisor d of m_b: T_minus(d) = sqrt(m_minus / d) + sqrt(d)   (Cheon 2006 Theorem 1 leading expression); T_plus(d)  = sqrt(m_plus / d) + d          (Cheon 2006 Theorem 2 leading expression; Theorem 2, not the 2006 abstract). e_b(d) = log2(T_b(d)) / log2(r). Admissible d is every positive divisor of m_b, including 1 and m_b. The two branches are never combined: no quantity in this amendment is a minimum over both branches."}

rows.effective_text: For every branch of every deployed row, construction control, C-BOUND state and null-arm sample, three fields are reported: bin, bin_at_least and boundary_flag, each with exactly the value given here. EXACT: bin is given by definitions.bins; bin_at_least equals bin; boundary_flag is as definitions.bins defines it. BOUND: let s be the depth of the witnessed upper bound and boundary_flag the flag that definitions.bins computes on s. If boundary_flag is false and s >= 3/4 + tau, bin is NEAR_FLOOR and bin_at_least is NEAR_FLOOR (the true value is at least as deep). Otherwise bin is UNDETERMINED and bin_at_least is the bin that definitions.bins gives an EXACT value of depth s (so a witnessed depth within tau of 3/4 gives UNDETERMINED, bin_at_least INTERMEDIATE and boundary_flag true). VOID: bin, bin_at_least and boundary_flag are all null. UNPINNED rows have no branches and report none of the three.
